newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends on positive note, most others too.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends on positive note, most others too.

text.p: Copper made steady upside progress on Thursday afternoon and ended firmly in the plus column after an early dip to five-month lows.
The other London Metal Exchange (LME) metals generally followed copper higher, reversing course from early softness.
Three months copper ended at $2,280 per tonne, compared to $2,267 at Wednesday's finish.
Meanwhile cash/threes backwardation softened to $135/$145, about $50 narrower than the previous day.
Shortcovering helped copper recover after prices tumbled in the pre-market to a low of $2,226, a new low since February 12.
A sizeable 13,025 tonne stock increase, following on the heels of Wednesday's 17,025-tonne stock rise, had initially put a dampener on the market.
"The stocks were a bit of a shock, and people were expecting prices to go to $2,200. But around $2,230 some consumer bargain hunting emerged followed by shortcovering," a trader said.
But resistance in a $2,290-$2,310 band may cap the market, he added, noting that copper turned back from a high of $2,288 during the afternoon kerb.
News that the majority of miners at the Neves Corvo copper mine had rejected a renewed company offer for implementing continuous working was mildly supportive.
However, a union leader said the strike would not be resumed if "dialogue" continued. Miners had shut the 107,000 tonnes per year metal content mine for five days last week over the dispute.
Zinc had surged to new highs since September 1990 earlier in the day, and it remained strong despite paring some of its gains.
By the end of the kerb it was $17 firmer at $1,511.
Aluminum also crept higher with copper, although traders said it was relatively ignored compared to copper and zinc. Prices were last at $1,579, up $9.
Nickel bounced off a low of $6,705 and made its way back above $6,800 resistance. It settled $80 firmer at $6,830 at the end of the kerb.
Lead bounced up $9 to $641, while alloy was indicated a touch firmer at $1,435/1,440.
The day's worst performer was tin, which failed to recover from fund liquidation and stop-loss selling on Wednesday.
It posted a fresh 2-1/3 year low of $5,420 in light volume trading, and ending the kerb barely different at $5,440, versus $5,450 on Wednesday.
